advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread the pass's repo_root into effective_status_map (via OutboundDiffConfig) so the status map is read from the SAME root as projects_mapping, matching fetcher._known_jira_statuses.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:278-281: `project_key = projects_store.resolve_project(ticket, mapping)` then `return config.effective_status_map(project_key)` — no root passed
config.py:77 `def effective_status_map(project_key: str, root: object = None)` and :97 `cfg = mc.load_mapping_config(root)`
config.py read_reserved_section(root=None) at src/rebar/config.py:616 falls back to `_discover_project_config(root)` (ambient discovery)
fetcher.py:170 `_known_jira_statuses(repo_root: Path)` DOES thread repo_root into load_mapping_config — the sibling path uses the correct root, this one does not
OutboundDiffConfig has no repo_root field (outbound_differ.py:235-252) and outbound_differ has no repo_root reference at all
advisory.finding: _effective_status_map_for resolves the effective status map by calling config.effective_status_map(project_key) with NO root argument, so mapping_config.load_mapping_config(root=None) re-reads config via ambient discovery (read_reserved_section falls back to cwd/user-path). This is inconsistent with the projects_mapping object the differ was handed (loaded from the pass's actual repo_root) and with fetcher._known_jira_statuses(repo_root), which threads repo_root explicitly. A pass whose cwd differs from the target repo may resolve a different/empty [mapping] block than the one that produced projects_mapping.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a repo_root to OutboundDiffConfig and pass it to config.effective_status_map(project_key, root=repo_root) in _effective_status_map_for.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile _LOCAL_STATUS_VOCAB with the actual reducer status vocabulary (add 'archived', decide 'cancelled' vs 'archived') and share ONE constant across inbound_fields / inbound_translate instead of a third literal.
evidence: inbound_fields.py:146 `{"idea", "open", "in_progress", "blocked", "closed", "cancelled", "deleted"}` with comment 'Source of truth: the ticket reducer's status processor'
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:33-35 `_KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES = frozenset({"idea", "open", "in_progress", "blocked", "closed", "archived", "deleted"})`
src/rebar/types.py:21 `TicketStatus = Literal["idea", "open", "in_progress", "blocked", "closed", "archived", "deleted"]`
inbound_translate.py:76-84 `_LOCAL_STATUS_VALUES` = (idea,open,in_progress,blocked,closed,cancelled,done) — a THIRD, different vocab set that the new helper does not reuse
advisory.finding: inbound_fields._LOCAL_STATUS_VOCAB documents its source of truth as 'the ticket reducer's status processor' but does not match it: the reducer's _KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES (and types.TicketStatus) = {idea,open,in_progress,blocked,closed,archived,deleted}, whereas the new vocab = {idea,open,in_progress,blocked,closed,cancelled,deleted} — it substitutes 'cancelled' for 'archived' and omits 'archived'. A rebar-status:archived annotation label would therefore be silently ignored by recover_status_label and fall back to the raw workflow status. The set also duplicates inbound_translate._LOCAL_STATUS_VALUES, which itself diverges (contains 'done', lacks 'deleted').

advisory.finding: resolve_outbound_status writes a warning to stderr unconditionally every time a local status has no target. It is invoked from the outbound diff on the CREATE and UPDATE paths per ticket per pass, with no dedup, so a persistent drifted status re-emits the warning on every ~20-minute pass and for every affected ticket — unlike the sibling _flag_unmapped_statuses path which deliberately dedups per-status and via a 24h alert_store window.
